reference: A 3×3 plot grid that grows to 5×5. Each year you play building and unit cards onto plots; buildings buff adjacent troops; rival kings' armies auto-battle you.
angle: The nine-plot kingdom fits one phone screen, and the existing async mode against eight rival kings is a ready-made PvP ladder.
signal: 1M+ copies; 13,850 peak CCU; 1.0 due Nov 2026; on Google Play's 2026 launch list

reference: Attacks are poker plays, and the defender must match or beat the same combo. Suits double as ability mana.
angle: The attack/defend poker exchange is a ready-made counter system; symmetric decks make fair, bluff-heavy PvP.

reference: Two layers: arrange brood chambers and pheromones in the underground nest to produce ants, then steer swarm flow across surface fronts.
angle: Split view: build the nest factory below, swipe to route swarm flow above — lane push with production-layout counterplay.

reference: Each move swaps your champion with units in its path and auto-fires an area attack at the destination. Three menu-free moves per round.
angle: Swipe-to-move-and-attack is pure touch input, and swaps displace enemy units too, turning PvP into a board-shuffling mind game.

reference: Racing autobattler: AI drivers race while you choose mid-race upgrades, tyres, pit stops and boosts as the weather changes.
angle: Race-engineer PvP: players make pit, tyre and boost calls for AI drivers in short races, with async ghost races.

reference: A tiny procedural floating island is the whole battlefield. Longboats land from any side; squads move tile to tile; burned houses lose you coin.
angle: Players alternate landing boat waves and placing squads on a one-screen island. Pike/sword/archer counters and terrain height decide fights.

reference: Poker hands score chips × mult; jokers stack additive and multiplicative modifiers, so build order beats hand luck.
angle: Hand score becomes damage, the joker draft becomes the build, and players race to a target.

reference: Vertical brick-breaker pit: ricochet balls up into descending enemy rows and fuse two ball types into evolved projectiles.
angle: Split-portrait PvP: rows you clear spill enemies into the rival's pit, and ball-fusion drafting is the build layer.

reference: Vertical pachinko board built from drafted triggers. Dropped balls chain triggers and spawn more balls for multiplying payouts against rising targets.
angle: Portrait-native: each player builds a board, and simultaneous drops convert payouts into damage under a shared timer.

reference: Turn-based 2v2 volleyball on a four-quadrant court. Back-row receives save stamina, front-row spikes hit harder; score on stamina zero or a dropped ball.
angle: Sports-court PvP with creature collection: tiny readable grid, short possessions, and online PvP already in.

reference: Each door offers three room blueprints to draft onto a 5×9 manor grid. A step budget and room resources constrain each day; the layout resets at dawn.
angle: Draft-a-tile battlefield: players alternately draft rooms from shared three-card offers, building the map their armies then fight across.
signal: 2M+ players incl. Game Pass/PS Plus; 19,243 peak CCU

reference: Three monkeys — one blind, one deaf, one mute — defuse cartoon bombs together in banana-yellow slapstick.
angle: Monkey bomb squads: pass, defuse and lob banana bombs between rival camps; each monkey's missing sense becomes a unit class.
signal: 1M copies in 2 weeks (studio); 22,936 peak CCU; #1 demo at June 2026 Next Fest

reference: A shotgun loaded with a shown mix of live and blank shells in hidden order. Items reveal shells, skip turns or double damage; a blank on yourself keeps your turn.
angle: A near-complete PvP chance device that already runs up to four players. Build units or lanes around the shell-risk turn.

reference: Tiny garden gnomes burgle human homes: furniture becomes terrain, stolen household items become crafted gear, and the gnomes break comically.
angle: Gnome gangs raid each other's houses: couch-cushion forts, thumbtack traps, kitchenware weapons — a tiny-scale household battlefield.

reference: Free-climbing an unclimbed summit: hand and foot placement on sheer rock, pitons, chalk, rationed supplies, clean cel-shaded comic look.
angle: Vertical race-battle up a cliff face: climb, drop rocks and cut ropes on rivals below; the summit as king-of-the-hill objective.

reference: Cats run a forgotten island post office: weigh, label and stamp parcels; at night moonlight reveals packages' magical properties.
angle: Cat courier rivals: deliver parcels across an island map while sabotaging opponents' routes; moonlit cursed-package power-ups.
signal: 200–300K units in July 2026; 9,036 peak CCU; followers ~18K (SteamDB, approx.)

reference: Brick-by-brick fortress building with structural integrity: load-bearing columns matter and collapses crush attackers and defenders alike. Build by day, hold at night.
angle: Async siege duel: build a wall blueprint, then a rival's army assaults it. Physics collapses make short, shareable replays.

reference: A slot machine is your only input: spin to meet escalating debt deadlines while charms rewrite symbol odds and pattern payouts.
angle: Spin-race PvP: both players chase a quota, drafting charms and spending spins to jinx the rival's reels.

reference: The Knucklebones minigame: place rolled dice in three columns. Matching dice multiply, and each die wipes same-value dice in the rival's facing column.
angle: A ready-made 60-second dice duel with real counterplay. Add unit or ability dice for a battle layer.

reference: Cabin crew of the world's worst airline: the plane falls apart mid-flight, illegal cargo breaks loose, difficult passengers, turbulence chaos.
angle: Rival budget airlines: each plane is a moving base; sabotage the enemy cabin with loose cargo, turbulence and unruly passengers.
signal: ~2M wishlists; #1 trending unreleased game (GameDiscoverCo, Jul 2026); ~500K wishlists in hours (studio claim)

reference: Buy naked humans with food, gear them into classes and watch them auto-fight. An async Tournament pits finished roguelike armies against each other.
angle: Run-to-army async PvP: a short roguelike draft builds a squad that fights other players' squads.

reference: Draft dice from a row and place them as invader units on a grid. Aligned pairs and multiples score; Chrono rerolls and Budge nudges throws.
angle: Contested draft row: take the die your rival needs, then align on your own grid. Turn-based and short.

reference: Your dice are your deck: roll, then place them in a 3×3 diamond grid. Colour sets attack or block, and neighbours modify each die.
angle: Simultaneous dice-placement duel: the small adjacency grid gives fast, readable counterplay on one screen.

reference: Vertical split: dig tunnels below for resources, then race back up to defend the dome before each timed wave. Has a Versus mode.
angle: Greed-vs-safety tempo duel: time spent mining is time undefended, and a rival's deliveries could fuel your next wave.
signal: 1M+ players; 6,487 peak CCU; iOS/Android port announced Sep 2026

reference: Visual node-programming of a golem party's behaviour — conditions, targeting, actions — then the automated party runs dungeons and bosses.
angle: Gambit-style rule cards as the PvP layer: duel logic sets, capped at three to five rule slots per unit for mobile.

reference: Combat items come from claw-machine pulls — weapons attack, armour blocks — and enemies tamper with the machine, e.g. flooding it so metal sinks.
angle: Sabotage-the-machine PvP: each player claws from their own cabinet while dropping hazards into the rival's.
signal: 245K copies incl. 80K on mobile; 2,790 peak CCU

reference: Blackjack duel where each side draws from its own custom deck. Bust and you take the rival's total as damage; otherwise you take the difference.
angle: Head-to-head blackjack is already PvP-shaped; overload and steal cards add counterplay to 30-second hands.
signal: 2,016 peak CCU; $1M+ gross in month one

reference: Tetromino maze-building tower defence: place block cards to shape enemy pathing, then towers; runes upgrade the blocks.
angle: Tetris-maze TD duel: send waves into each other's mazes, Legion TD style; drafted block pieces are the PvP resource.
signal: 97% of 4,213 reviews positive (1.0 after EA since 2024)

reference: Tarkov-style extraction survival in a world of armed ducks: cute top-down duck soldiers in gritty military kit, hideout building, heavy loot.
angle: Duck-army skins for top-down squad shooters or tower battles; cute animals in gritty kit is a strong, ad-friendly contrast.
signal: 4.3M units by Nov 2025; 301,322 peak CCU; followers ~129K (SteamDB, approx.)

reference: Mercenary club management around arena fights: a simulated transfer market, leagues and cups; auto-battle or captain control; async Challenge Tower.
angle: Football-manager meta for autobattlers: seasonal leagues and a player-driven merc market as the PvP economy and retention layer.

reference: Evolve a creature through a living ecosystem, stacking 125+ evolutions; the title riffs on the carcinisation meme.
angle: Evolution arena: mutate creatures mid-match with draftable body parts trending toward armoured crab forms; a memeable ad hook.

reference: Robot cowboys hunting bounties in a haunted Wild West: six-shooters plus fireballs, reanimated skeletons, haunted mines, a giant ghost train.
angle: Weird-West robot gunslingers: duels mixing revolvers and spells, with the ghost train as a roaming arena hazard.
signal: 1.3M copies incl. keys (May 2026); 47,256 peak CCU; followers ~94K (SteamDB, approx.)

reference: Program a three-homunculus team by placing ability flasks on each unit's turn timeline; fights play out as scripted, against async player ghosts.
angle: Drag-to-slot timeline programming is touch-native, and revealed enemy timelines allow counter-programming on a ranked ladder.

reference: Your train is both deck and battlefield anchor: the locomotive, carriages and driver add cards. Enemies close from several sides; shove them off cliffs or the track.
angle: Train-as-base duel: carriage choice is both deck and formation, and raiders target specific cars, so composition doubles as positioning.

reference: Runs climb through other players' phantom armies, and whoever dethrones the Fool King issues decrees that change the rules for everyone else.
angle: Weekly champion's decree: the top player sets a global rule modifier for everyone's async battles — live-ops built into the ruleset.

reference: Trapped in a doomed city as a monster tornado approaches: scavenge parts, fix your van, escape escalating disasters and total destruction.
angle: The tornado as a shrinking-zone storm: fleeing teams fix vans, grab loot and let flying debris hit rivals.
signal: 200–300K units in July 2026; 6,718 peak CCU; followers ~31K (SteamDB, approx.)

reference: Chess on shrunken boards where you must capture every enemy piece. The board decays if you take too many moves. Buy rule-bending pieces and tiles.
angle: Mini-chess PvP with the decaying board as a shot clock and rule-bending piece drafts between rounds.

reference: A radial engine board: 18 fuel items across three rings × six segments, where ring and segment adjacency drive synergies.
angle: A circular loadout replaces the backpack grid; rotating rings between rounds re-aligns synergies — distinctive and thumb-friendly.

reference: Your castle layout is your army: placing buildings in the fortress grid unlocks units and heroes, then async autobattles against other players' castles.
angle: Base-layout-as-deck async PvP: quick castle edits between rounds against ghost castles; shareable layouts drive the meta.

reference: Hex autobattler where heroes respec across roles — backline healer into tank — via 180 specialisations and 500+ level-up paths. No timers.
angle: Role-morph drafting: the same pick branches to counter the opponent's comp, adding a counter layer to board PvP.
signal: 16,751 followers; ~230K wishlists; #1 Steam demo for ~2 months

reference: Inventory slots are a synergy puzzle feeding auto-resolved fights. A new boss every three days forces counter-builds. PvP is best-of-five on identical seeds.
angle: A proven loop: same-seed runs, build between stages, clash at stage end. Ghost opponents give an async fallback.

reference: Turn-based overworld; battles are real-time autobattles of hundreds of units where you only cast spells and give broad orders.
angle: Composition duel where the only live input is a spell hand: draft armies, then time spells during a short mass clash.

reference: Cartoon castaways crash-land on islands and fish with rods and guns: ragdoll fish, trick-shot bonuses, boss fish, island-hopping gear upgrades.
angle: Island-vs-island angler duels: reel ragdoll fish, then fling or shoot them at the rival boat; boss fish as mid-match objectives.
signal: 6.3M+ units in August 2026; 1M in 2 days; 373,971 peak CCU

reference: Ship modules produce resources and keep the engines running; aliens breach the hull at telegraphed times and places; you build kill zones.
angle: Telegraphed-breach PvP: the attacker picks breach points and timing, the defender pre-builds kill zones — bluffing plus economy tempo.

reference: Build a pachinko board: upgrade pegs to split balls, pull with gravity wells, explode or return to top; mod the balls; choose where to drop for chains.
angle: Vertical peg board as battlefield: each player builds half, and drops cascade into the opponent's side. One-tap drop timing.

reference: 1v1 turn-based hex arena with no dice: actions resolve exactly as previewed. Win through zones, sponsor objectives or crowd approval.
angle: Deterministic duels with several win conditions; zone control and a crowd meter reward tempo over luck in short ranked matches.

reference: A side-on illuminated-manuscript page is the battlefield. Draw beasts with ink, shove units off the page edges, and dodge hazards like Hell's Maws.
angle: Turn-based 1v1 on one illustrated page: ink as mana, ring-outs off the margins. Already ships hot-seat PvP.

reference: Four-column lane card duel. Damage tips a tooth scale instead of HP and you win at a five-point lead; you sacrifice cards to pay costs.
angle: The scale-lead tug-of-war gives three-minute lane duels. Sacrifice-for-tempo and column blocking carry cleanly to touch.

reference: Crewing a 5,000-ton dieselpunk turret in alternate-history 1920s Spain: teleprinter orders, ballistic maps, 30+ shell types, a heavy analog cockpit.
angle: Dieselpunk artillery duels: each player commands a colossal turret-fortress; choose shells, read the map, out-range the rival's nest.
signal: 650K units in Aug 2026; 17,599 peak CCU; 97% positive

reference: Seat characters on buses, in cinemas and at weddings so each one's preferences and pet peeves are met — a pure adjacency-constraint puzzle.
angle: Alternate-seating PvP: place units to satisfy your own side's adjacency rules while spoiling the rival's.
signal: 1,713 peak CCU; 97% positive; Best Mobile Game, 2026 NY Game Awards

reference: Side-scrolling single-lane kingdom with a one-input coin economy: drop coins to recruit, build and upgrade walls. Night waves hit both flanks.
angle: Horizontal lane with the base in the centre and fronts on both sides. Coin-drop is ideal one-thumb input for a territory-push duel.

reference: Turn-based autobattler where you place and rotate units on an expandable grid to aim their talents, with towers and a shop between fights.
angle: Facing adds a second placement axis: rotating one unit counters a formation without any micro.

reference: Cramped grid arenas with three momentum per turn. Shove and redirect enemies so their telegraphed attacks hit allies or hazards.
angle: Small-arena positioning duel: telegraphed intents let players bait friendly fire and ring-outs. Short turns suit async play.

reference: Reverse dungeon crawl: heroes walk a fixed chain of trap, monster and spell rooms you fill. Kill them or break their morale.
angle: Async gauntlet PvP: build a room chain and a rival's party runs it. Dual HP/morale win paths create counter-picks.

game: Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!
reference: Tidying an arcane magic library: shelve 3,072 scattered books, unlock spells as rows complete; flying tomes, enchanted stacks.
angle: Wizard-librarian duels: sort flying spellbooks onto your shelves to charge spells, hurl misfiled tomes at rivals; cozy-magic art.

reference: Side-scrolling god game: a hand-of-god cursor lifts villagers and objects and reshapes terrain to defend settlements at night.
angle: Finger-as-hand deploy on a side-on lane: pick up and drop units directly — native touch interaction.

reference: A hero auto-walks a looping road while you place terrain and enemy tiles around it. Tile adjacency combos reshape each lap's fights.
angle: Plant threat tiles on the rival's loop while buffing your own: auto-battle races decided by placement, not micro.

game: Master Healer Kale with useless party
reference: You play only the healer: an AI tank, archer and mage autobattle while you cast heals, buffs and 18 support spells.
angle: Support-only PvP: each player keeps an autobattling trio alive with tap-heals and buffs — skill without precision aiming.

reference: Blank white mannequin bodies you spray-paint to match the stage, hiding in plain sight with poses while hunters scan the scene.
angle: Paint-your-hero camouflage: units recolour to terrain, and blank-canvas avatars double as cosmetics and a spot-the-hider ad hook.

reference: Breeding a cat army across generations — genetics, mutations and inherited traits — in a crude, cute-grotesque cartoon style.
angle: Cat-squad army or auto-battler: breed and mutate cats for inherited abilities. Tone the crude humour down for mainstream ads.

reference: 4v4 prop hunt where the clock flips roles: at midnight the ghosts become supercharged and the hunters must survive a timed counter-assault.
angle: Scheduled role reversal: the attacker becomes the defender at a known time, so players bank advantage and position for the flip.

reference: An isometric road-bound city that never stops moving. You bolt defensive districts and towers onto the travelling town at shelters.
angle: Moving-fortress race: two cities on parallel roads stack towers onto themselves and redirect monster waves at each other.

reference: 1930s rubber-hose cartoon noir: hand-drawn black-and-white animation, a jazz-age mouse detective, Cuphead-style enemies in a first-person shooter.
angle: Rubber-hose cartoon arena: 1930s black-and-white animation dressing a hero shooter or squad battler — instantly distinctive in ads.
signal: 1M+ copies all platforms (Jul 2026); ~350K Steam units / $10M+ in April; 13,755 peak CCU

reference: Sensor warfare: active radar reveals the emitter, ships run cold to hide, asteroids cast radar shadows and jamming blinds sensors.
angle: Battleship-style hidden-information duel: every scan also exposes you, so ping-or-hide timing becomes the mind game.

reference: Build drones from 75+ physics parts plus sensor and logic wiring. Competitive arenas pit your autonomous drone against other players' drones.
angle: Build-then-watch async PvP: snap together parts and simple logic, then the drones fight on their own.

reference: An end-of-times heatwave; strangers knock at night and you inspect tells — eyes, teeth, armpits — to judge human or doppelgänger.
angle: Doorstep social deduction: send disguised visitor units to rival houses; defenders inspect tells and decide who gets in.

reference: Settlement placement is the draft: buildings near resources and terrain boost output and warband; re-layout each round; god blessings bought with a second currency.
angle: Adjacency-placement puzzle each round feeding async raids and defences; the dual currency creates tempo-vs-power choices.

reference: You are a pathogen inside a human host: a microscopic procedural world, organelle upgrades, battles against immune-system cells.
angle: Germ vs germ: rival pathogens race to infect an organ while dodging white-cell hazards; cell-biology art gives clean, colourful unit reads.
signal: 100K copies in week one; 200–300K units in July 2026; 5,893 peak CCU

reference: Eight-player autobattler built on Texas Hold'em: everyone sees the same community cards, and relics that alter suits, ranks and scoring split the builds.
angle: Shared-board poker PvP from an established mobile publisher: same information, divergent relic builds. Watch as a competitor.

reference: Each ingredient is a fixed vector that moves a marker across a hidden alchemy map. Chain them to land on effect zones while dodging hazards.
angle: Vector-path race: draft ingredients to steer markers to shared targets, bumping or blocking each other's routes.
signal: 10,161 peak CCU; on Google Play's 2026 launch list

reference: Commanding a zombie-outbreak checkpoint: inspect survivors for infection signs — coughs, bites, scans — manage supplies and hold the wall.
angle: Checkpoint defence: opponents smuggle disguised infected units into your line; scan, quarantine or shoot before they breach.

reference: Coin-pusher roguelike: shoot coins at a moving pusher to shove others into the scoring zone and hit a round quota. Special coins explode or duplicate.
angle: Shared pusher tray: your shots shove coins toward your own edge and away from the rival's.

reference: Swipe to recruit; a four-unit hand spins around a central core. Rotate units to shield your core and break the rival's. Online ranked PvP.
angle: The rotation-formation duel suits swipe and already ships ranked PvP. Weak reception, so take the mechanic, not the execution.

reference: A mid-2000s Tokyo repair shop restoring retro consoles, flip phones and music players, with customer stories. Y2K tech nostalgia.
angle: Y2K gadget brawlers: restored flip phones, handhelds and MP3 players as upgradable units, with a screwdriver-repair loop between rounds.

reference: Side-scrolling Dracula castle rebuilt room by room between assaults; room placement forms chokepoints; monster army plus Dracula's own abilities.
angle: Side-on castle cross-section — Monster Train floors turned sideways: arrange rooms, then raid rival castles async.
signal: 10,229 followers; #2 upcoming Auto Battler by wishlists; from the Cataclismo team

reference: 1v1 duels where the loser of each round picks a permanent power-up card; stacked cards turn weapon and body into escalating builds.
angle: Loser-drafts keeps matches close. Pair it with auto-combat to remove real-time aiming.

reference: Friends physics-drive a rickety RV home through wilderness canyons — winching, pushing, fixing and crashing; the vehicle is the whole team's base.
angle: Moving-base race-battle: each team's RV is its base; upgrade it, winch it and ram rivals off canyon roads.

reference: A one-dimensional lane of 5–9 tiles with visible enemy intents. Move, turn or queue up to three attacks, and trick enemies into hitting each other.
angle: The 1D lane suits portrait. Simultaneous-reveal turns with queued attacks make a readable three-minute duel.

game: Sir, We Have an Orc Problem
reference: Orc hordes flow across the map like liquid; place turrets and tune each firing arc, then reposition between incremental runs.
angle: Horde-as-fluid defence: aim arcs at flowing masses, with PvP by sending flows at each other's defences. Tap-to-rotate turrets.
signal: ~128K units / ~$1.05M gross by 4 Aug (dev figures); 87% of 4,193 reviews positive

reference: Spin a 3×3 slot machine to summon random units; sacrifice weak units to evolve others; items and cores bias the odds.
angle: Slot-reel summoning as the deploy system: spin, hold, nudge; odds-bending items become counterplay in short defence duels.
signal: 4,492 followers; store page discloses AI-generated art

reference: Slot reels are the combat system: three daggers attack, three shields block, three coins pay. Buy reels and symbols between fights.
angle: Reel duel: both spin at once and matched lines trade damage. Reel-building replaces deckbuilding and suits one thumb.

reference: Each step you choose one of four rows, then land on a random tile in it — monster, chest or trap. Items rewrite the odds.
angle: Partial-control chance device: both players pick rows on a shared board and seed traps into each other's likely lanes.

reference: 2D side-scroller marching left to right through alternating outposts and six-slot forts. Orders only reach troops within hearing range of the hero.
angle: Landscape siege lane with build slots in each captured fort. A command-radius banner could replace micro in a side-on push duel.

reference: Combat resolves by spinning slot reels built from collected symbols; symbol synergies set each spin's damage and defence.
angle: Simultaneous slot duel: reel-building controls variance, giving readable but skill-expressive rounds.

reference: A shared timeline shows when every action lands. Hitting a foe before it acts staggers it and can cancel its attack.
angle: Simultaneous-plan duels: both players queue actions on one timeline and race to interrupt. Fast-weak vs slow-strong is the counter system.

reference: Roguelite kingdom on a giant walking crab's back: odd-shaped buildings compete for shell space, 100+ units, tower-defence combat.
angle: Walking-base battlefield: a polyomino city on a marching creature, with PvP as two creature-cities colliding.
signal: 1,122 followers ~12 days after 16 Sep reveal; from the King is Watching team

reference: A grid kingdom where only buildings inside the king's movable gaze produce. You slide the gaze to juggle economy, troops and walls.
angle: Attention as the PvP resource: drag your gaze between economy and front line while rival attacks force you to look away.

reference: A picture-book battlefield where placed cards march toward the enemy base. Any card that reaches the base is permanently removed from your deck.
angle: Lane-push PvP with permanent attrition: every breakthrough costs a unit for good, forcing timing and sacrifice decisions.

reference: A city built on the back of Onbu, a giant walking creature. Its health, its trust in you and its route through hostile biomes shape your base.
angle: Base-on-colossus frame: two walking titans clash while players build and defend settlements on their backs.

reference: Spend a gold budget placing wobbly-physics units against a visible enemy army, then watch unscripted ragdoll combat with no control after the start.
angle: Blind-budget deploy PvP: both players place armies at once and physics decides. Pure composition and placement, no micro.

reference: The train advances nonstop; players harvest wood and iron and craft rails just ahead of it. One tool per type forces role splits. 2v2 Versus race.
angle: Mirrored-lane race: harvest and lay track faster than your rival while your own train keeps coming. Sabotage cards would add interaction.

reference: Drive a rolling castle across an isometric map. Swallowing villages bolts cannon, arcane and explosive siege modules onto its silhouette.
angle: Castle-snake arena: grow a modular fortress by eating neutral targets, then ram and out-gun rival castles. Simplify driving to path choice.
signal: 10,568 peak CCU; 250K+ pre-launch wishlists; 77% of 887 reviews positive

reference: Side-on landscape lane. Units auto-advance, take cover and fight over a shifting frontline; destruction reshapes cover; airstrikes and missiles are support calls.
angle: Direct template for a 1v1 lane tug-of-war: pick composition and support-strike timing, no micro, and push the front into the enemy base.
